A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same PredFormer work. All 11 pages of v3 and 21 pages of v4, including appendices, are readable and matchable across the substantial reformatting; essential text, equations, tables and figures are available.

before.justification: Sections 4.1–4.5 and Tables 2–8 report original PredFormer prediction results and architectural ablations across four benchmarks.

after.justification: The original empirical results are retained, with additional memory measurements, recurrent-model comparisons and patch-size ablation results in Tables 2–5 and 11–13.

M1.justification: Patch embedding and recovery, sinusoidal positional encoding, SwiGLU-based gated transformer blocks and the nine attention configurations are retained. The new partition-counting algorithm analyzes existing variants; it does not change the prediction procedure.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate Moving MNIST, Human3.6m, TaxiBJ and WeatherBench-S/T2m for the same object-motion, human-video, traffic-flow and temperature-prediction tasks. The added appendix experiments reuse this coverage.

E2.justification: Appendix Tables 11–12 add VMRNN to comparisons on Moving MNIST and TaxiBJ. VMRNN was only discussed in v3; SwinLSTM was already evaluated. Comparator membership in the four main benchmark tables is retained.

E3.justification: v4 adds a controlled Triplet-TST patch-size comparison, memory-use evaluation and epoch-time comparisons. Table 3 revises the reported Human3.6m OpenSTL-ViT size from 28.3M to 11.0M parameters, without establishing whether experiments were rerun. Original splits, horizons and default training settings remain. A.3's new equal-unit normalization conflicts with the retained equal-GTB description, so an actual depth change is not established.

E4.justification: A.5.2/Table 13 adds a focused patch-size sensitivity test, comparing prediction accuracy and computational cost for patches of size 4 and 8. A.8/Table 15 adds a partition-count versus performance analysis. Existing depth, gating, positional-encoding and regularization ablations and visual case studies are retained.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, random seeds, uncertainty intervals, error bars or significance tests. The new combinatorial partition counts are not uncertainty estimates.

E6.justification: v4 adds memory results across all four benchmarks, VMRNN and training-time comparisons, patch-size outcomes and partition counts. Original main-table predictive scores are retained, but Human3.6m OpenSTL-ViT resource entries change from 28.3M/239.0G/17 FPS to 11.0M/142.2G/35 FPS. New appendix entries also contain discrepancies: Table 11 reports six-layer Moving MNIST MSE 12.5 while Table 2 retains 12.4; these do not establish a same-setting performance change.

T1.justification: New Appendix A.3 derives compute and memory complexity for the nine variants and CNN/RNN baseline families, summarized in Table 9. A.8/Figure 8 introduces a formal partition-counting procedure to support a representational-capacity hypothesis. These substantial analytical additions go beyond v3's retained architecture equations, task definition and tensor transformations.

C1.justification: The abstract and introduction retain the central architecture, nine-variant and four-benchmark claims. The conclusion narrows broad temporal-first superiority to dataset-dependent tendencies, particularly for longer horizons, and explicitly adds memory efficiency to its claims. This qualifies the conclusions without redefining the main contribution.

C2.justification: A.7–A.8 substantially expand explanations of variant performance through temporal horizons, spatial/temporal token ratios and partition diversity, beyond v3's general dataset-dependence discussion. A.5.2 also explains the default patch size through an accuracy–cost tradeoff. Some new interpretations are questionable: A.8's claimed TaxiBJ ordering contradicts Table 15.

D1.justification: The abstract changes code and trained models from a promised release to a reported release, and v4 adds a project-page pointer. Tables 11–12 disclose epoch times, and Section 4.5 expands variant/depth selection guidance. Core implementation and default hyperparameters remain, with v3 Table 9 becoming v4 Table 10.

R1.justification: The same 43 cited works and the main CNN/RNN/ViT positioning are retained. VMRNN was already cited and discussed in v3; its new experimental participation changes E2. Switching from numbered to author–year references does not add related work.

P1.justification: Most existing prose and the main section order are retained. The conclusion is rewritten, variant-selection guidance is expanded, and the original supplementary Sections 6–9 become Appendix A subsections alongside new content. Author, affiliation, publication-header and citation-style edits are also present.

P2.justification: The document changes from two columns to a single-column journal layout, substantially resizing and relocating existing displays. Tables 2–5 gain memory columns; new Tables 9 and 11–15 and Figure 8 present complexity, experiments and analyses. The original hyperparameter table is retained as Table 10, and Figure 4's caption is corrected to Moving MNIST.

improvement.justification: The added memory measurements, VMRNN comparisons and controlled patch-size ablation make efficiency and design choices easier to assess, while the conclusion is more appropriately scoped. These provide a limited quality gain over v3. New appendix inconsistencies constrain that gain: A.3's equal-unit normalization conflicts with retained GTB budgets, and A.8's TaxiBJ ranking disagrees with Table 15, weakening the added theoretical explanations.
